full_judgment:
"The plaint is no evidence for the proof of the case of the plaintiff. The absence of the defendant who asked for adjournment but refused on reasons assigned therefor can not give occasion for the plaintiff to obtain ex parte decree without producing the relevant documents on the basis of which relief is sought for. The court is bound to apply its mind with reference to the pleadings and satisfy itself as to what should be the proper proof for passing a decree on the basis of averments made in the plaint". 

 8. In view of the above decisions in the above cases, we find that the Labour Court, not being Court of Appeal over the domestic proceeding conducted by the employer,'' while passing of the ex parte decree, being a Civil Court, ought to have been satisfied on legal material that the inquiry proceeding was not conducted following the Rules and the principle of natural justice on the basis of averments in the Complaint petition. In the absence of such finding we are of the view that in an ex parte hearing the Labour Court could not pass a decision mechanically stating that upon perusal on the Complaint Petition and the exhibited papers filed, the case is proved.
